sections.summary: Completed in an earlier run of this track and verified intact at resume. `PullRequestRootResolver` in src/main/pullRequestRoots.ts does two-stage resolution (tier 1 remembered root, tier 2 open session roots, tier 3 approvedRoots — no folder walk; the folderIndex catalog only on a full-stage miss), keyed by normalized URL in a module-level promise map with a 5 s TTL after settle, plus a 60 s remotes cache and a 60 s per-slug negative cache. `previewPullRequestFolder` stats the remembered folder or joins a live resolution and otherwise returns null — it never walks and never spawns. `applyExternalReview` races a quick resolution against a 150 ms deadline and ships the resolved root with the openExternalPullRequest payload, so the renderer's resolve is a lookup.

sections.summary: All eleven items implemented. (1) Multicast flights: new src/main/pullRequestFlights.ts holds a `PullRequestReviewFlight` that records metadata / pages / replace / checks / done, fans each event to every subscriber (isolating a throwing one), and replays the whole sequence synchronously to a late joiner — a `replace` supersedes the pages it replaced. `#reviewFlights` now maps selector -> flight and `#reviewAborts` became `#reviewRequests` (requestId -> flight) with the AbortController owned by the flight and refcounted through `attach`/`detach`, so a fetch two tabs are reading ends only when the last one cancels and a warmup never keeps it alive. (2) URL-keyed cache index: `PullRequestReviewCache` writes `<sha1('index', normalizedUrl)>.latest.json` next to each diff (`readIndex`, `#writeIndex`, `#indexPath` normalizes both spellings of the URL); sweep excludes index files from the entry count and caps them by mtime; a stale pointer self-heals into a normal fetch. `#openCachedPullRequestReview` reads index -> entry and emits metadata + one files page + done with no `gh` call at all — it even works when `gh` cannot be found. (3) Parallel hops: `gh pr diff` starts alongside the metadata hop through the new `#collectPullRequestDiff` (returns complete | aborted | too-large), its pages staged until the metadata event opens the view. (4) Lean metadata: PULL_REQUEST_REVIEW_FIELDS dropped `files`, `statusCheckRollup` and `mergeable`; a background `#loadPullRequestChecks` emits `{ kind: 'checks' }` and folds into the stored summary. (5) `#seedPullRequestIdentity` seeds `#pullRequestIdentities` from the metadata, and `changedFiles > 300` aborts the doomed single diff document and pages the files API instead. (6) Warmup never steals — `primePullRequest` passes `intent: 'warmup'`. (7) `pendingPullRequestUrl` on the restore hint; boot.tsx preloads MultiFileReview instead of the cached view's chunk on a Cmd+H launch. (8) Verified already in place. (9) Dead `cancelPullRequestReview(requestId)` deleted; retargeting a New tab now cancels the review it abandons. (10) Raycast `lib/horus.ts` rewritten around a pure `horusLaunchPlan` with `pgrep -x Horus`, and the deep link is dispatched before `closeMainWindow`. (11) MAX_PULL_REQUEST_CACHE_ENTRIES 20 -> 60.

sections.deviations: 1. Item 9's "abort the previous foreground flight when a different PR arrives" lives in the renderer (openPullRequestFromLocator cancels the outstanding request of the tab it retargets) rather than in RepositoryService: main cannot tell a retarget from a second tab, and aborting a flight another world is still reading would break that tab. The main-side half is the refcounted attach/detach. 2. The cached open emits one files page instead of re-chunking the stored patch — it is already complete and chunking only helps a stream. 3. #openCachedPullRequestReview runs before getGhExecutable() so a cached review opens even where gh is missing. 4. reviewNotes:
Not measured — the whole point of the track is unverified until the reviewer builds and probes. Nothing here has been run against the installed build: no pr-open-probe, no git/gh spawn shim count. The four claims that need measuring are warm cached <= 400 ms to `.multi-file-review`, cold cached <= 1,500 ms, uncached shell < 900 ms, and exactly 2 `gh` spawns on a cached hit (headRefOid revalidate + checks). The first open of any PR after this change still takes the slow path because no `.latest.json` pointer exists yet; the probe must open each PR twice and measure the second.

Deliberate design decision worth a second opinion — when the cache index hits, the flight's promise stays pending until the background `gh pr view --json headRefOid` revalidation settles (~400-600 ms), even though the renderer has painted from the streamed events at ~40 ms. Resolving earlier would tear down the renderer's progress listener in its `finally` and lose the `replace` event. Consequence: the patch world sits at `loadStatus: 'loading'` for those few hundred ms with content already on screen. `isPullRequestWorkspacePending` returns false once files exist, so no blocking spinner, but I could not verify every consumer of `loadStatus === 'loading'` in MultiFileReview / PullRequestReviewBar for a subtler indicator.

Known wart I chose not to fix, documented in the progress log: on a `replace` (force push while the tab is open) the world keeps the `worldId` it was opened with, so it no longer equals `patchWorldId(currentReview)`. Rekeying would orphan the navigation and view caches and strand the in-flight loader, which holds the old id in a closure. Consequence: reopening the same pull request after a force push, while the updated tab is still open, creates a second tab. Fixing it properly means identity matching in `openPatchWorld`, which is Track E/C territory.

Risky spots. (a) `#fetchPullRequestReview` now runs `gh pr diff` concurrently with `gh pr view` and stages its pages until the metadata event; on a legacy oid-keyed cache hit the diff is aborted and the staged pages dropped. The abort ordering is covered by a `finally`, but the concurrency is not unit-tested — it needs a real `gh`. (b) `changedFiles > 300` now skips `gh pr diff` entirely and pages the files API; this changes behaviour for large PRs and is untested against a real large pull request. (c) `viewerCanSubmitDecision` on the cached path comes from the stored index unless this process already resolved the viewer login, to avoid a third spawn — it goes stale if the user switches `gh` accounts between sessions. (d) `mergeContentSearchResults` puts the open file's extra hits after the 24 repository hits, so the palette's first eight rows are unchanged; if Track C ever renders more than the cap this ordering should be revisited.

Cross-track items left for their owners. Track C, `useRepositorySearch.ts`: nothing passes `forOpenPath` yet, so with the repository cap now 24 the DiffSurface markers for the open file are less complete than before until that call is wired. Track C, `App.tsx` ~line 702: `const open = (url: string)` should take the resolved root from `onOpenExternalPullRequest` and pass it as `preferredRoot`.

Shared-file discipline: every touch of `src/main/repository.ts`, `src/main/index.ts`, `src/shared/contracts.ts` and `src/renderer/src/boot.tsx` was an exact-string Edit, never a rewrite.
